title: Meta Pixels
content:
# Meta Pixels

Create, read, rename and share a Meta Pixel, manage its users and custom conversions, read stats and diagnostics, and install it on Shopify or WordPress.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

Use `GET` and `POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags` to list an ads account's pixels and create new ones. Conversion campaigns, website audiences and server-side events all point at a pixel.

## Before you start

Zernio exposes pixels under the platform-neutral tracking tags API, where `kind` is `pixel` on Meta.

It runs on the Meta ads account you already connected, so there is no extra consent screen. `accountId` is that ads account.

The `act_<n>` ad account ids come from [`GET /v1/ads/accounts`](/platforms/meta-ads/connect#find-your-ad-account-id).

## Read the tag

`GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags` lists every pixel the connected ads account can see.

Run it first. The pixel a campaign needs usually exists already, and the create below is not idempotent.

Add `adAccountId` to scope the list to one ad account. Omit it and each name carries the ad account it was discovered on. The list omits `code`.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: existing } = await zernio.trackingtags.listTrackingTags({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d' },
  query: { adAccountId: 'act_1234567890' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

existing = client.tracking_tags.list_tracking_tags(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="act_1234567890",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags?adAccountId=act_1234567890" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": "1729525464415281",
      "name": "Website pixel",
      "platform": "metaads",
      "kind": "pixel",
      "status": "active",
      "lastFiredTime": 1804150800,
      "installed": true,
      "creationTime": 1804064400,
      "ownerBusinessId": "1049283746152738",
      "ownerAdAccountId": "act_1234567890"
    }
  ]
}
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags/{tagId}` returns one pixel with the same fields plus its install `code`. `tagId` is the numeric pixel id, which is also the `siteTagId` the site loads.

## Create a pixel

`adAccountId` and `name` are the only inputs. Meta owns the pixel through the Business Manager that owns the ad account.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: created } = await zernio.trackingtags.createTrackingTag({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d' },
  body: { adAccountId: 'act_1234567890', name: 'Website pixel' }
});

const pixelId = created.tag.id;
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
created = client.tracking_tags.create_tracking_tag(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="act_1234567890",
    name="Website pixel",
)

pixel_id = created["tag"]["id"]
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "adAccountId": "act_1234567890", "name": "Website pixel" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "tag": {
    "id": "1729525464415281",
    "name": "Website pixel",
    "platform": "metaads",
    "kind": "pixel",
    "status": "active",
    "code": "<script>!function(f,b,e,v,n,t,s){...}</script>",
    "lastFiredTime": null,
    "installed": false,
    "creationTime": 1804064400,
    "ownerBusinessId": "1049283746152738",
    "ownerAdAccountId": "act_1234567890"
  }
}
```

`tag.id` is the pixel id. Use it for:

- `promotedObject.pixelId` on [conversion campaigns](/platforms/meta-ads/conversion-campaigns)
- `pixelId` on a [website audience](/platforms/meta-ads/audiences#website-audiences)
- `destinationId` on the [Conversions API](/platforms/meta-ads/conversions)

Creating a pixel does not install it. Put `code` on the site, or skip the snippet and send events server-side, which a new pixel accepts immediately.

`installed` is derived from `lastFiredTime`, so a `null` there means the pixel has never fired.

<Callout type="warn">
The create is not idempotent: every call makes another pixel. Never auto-retry one. On a `502`, confirm with `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags` before sending it again.
</Callout>

A `400` means an invalid `adAccountId`, an ad account outside a Business Manager, or the per-business pixel cap.

## Rename and update

`PATCH /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags/{tagId}` updates a whitelist of fields. Send at least one of them:

- `name`
- `enableAutomaticMatching` (Meta's Advanced Matching)
- `automaticMatchingFields`
- `firstPartyCookieStatus`
- `dataUseSetting`

`automaticMatchingFields` takes Meta's terse codes: `em` email, `ph` phone, `fn` first name, `ln` last name, `ge` gender, `db` date of birth, `ct` city, `st` state, `zp` ZIP, `country` and `external_id`.

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/1729525464415281" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "Website pixel (renamed)", "enableAutomaticMatching": true }'
```

Response (`200`), the re-fetched tag:

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "tag": {
    "id": "1729525464415281",
    "name": "Website pixel (renamed)",
    "kind": "pixel",
    "status": "active",
    "lastFiredTime": 1804150800,
    "installed": true
  }
}
```

**There is no delete.** Meta has no API for it: `AdsPixel` has no delete in Meta's Business SDK, and `DELETE /{pixel}` answers "Unsupported delete request" (code 100, subcode 33).

To stop using a pixel, unshare it or disable it in Events Manager.

## Share a pixel with another ad account

A pixel works only in the ad account it was created on until you share it. Sharing lets another account's campaigns and audiences use it.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
await zernio.trackingtags.addTrackingTagSharedAccount({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', tagId: '1729525464415281' },
  body: { adAccountId: 'act_9876543210' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
client.tracking_tags.add_tracking_tag_shared_account(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    tag_id="1729525464415281",
    ad_account_id="act_9876543210",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/1729525464415281/shared-accounts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "adAccountId": "act_9876543210" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{ "platform": "metaads", "ok": true }
```

`GET` on the same path returns `sharedAccounts[]` with each account's `id`, `name` and `businessId`. `DELETE` removes one.

**No Business Manager.** A pixel created on an ad account that no Business Manager owns comes back with `ownerBusinessId: null`.

It cannot be shared at all, because Meta rejects the share. Claim the ad account into a Business Manager first.

These endpoints share pixels with ad accounts. People and partner businesses are under [Users and partners](#users-and-partners).

## Users and partners

A Business Manager pixel has people and system users with access, and partner businesses it is shared with.

| Call | Does |
|------|------|
| `GET .../tracking-tags/{tagId}/users` | Lists the users |
| `POST .../tracking-tags/{tagId}/users` | Assigns one |
| `GET .../tracking-tags/{tagId}/partners` | Lists the partners |

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
await zernio.trackingtags.assignTrackingTagUser({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', tagId: '1729525464415281' },
  body: { userId: '122101234567890123', tasks: ['ANALYZE', 'ADVERTISE'] }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
client.tracking_tags.assign_tracking_tag_user(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    tag_id="1729525464415281",
    user_id="122101234567890123",
    tasks=["ANALYZE", "ADVERTISE"],
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/1729525464415281/users" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "userId": "122101234567890123", "tasks": ["ANALYZE", "ADVERTISE"] }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "platform": "metaads", "userId": "122101234567890123", "tasks": ["ANALYZE", "ADVERTISE"] }
```

- `userId` is the business-scoped user id from `GET /v1/ads/businesses/users`.
- `tasks` are Meta's pixel tasks: `AA_ANALYZE`, `ADVERTISE`, `ANALYZE`, `EDIT` and `UPLOAD`. Anything else answers `400`.
- Assigning a user who already has access replaces their tasks.
- The list returns `users[]` with `id`, `name` and `tasks`.
- A pixel on a personal ad account has no business, so its list is empty and an assign answers `400`.
- Both need the `business_management` permission on the connecting Meta user, who must be an admin of the business that owns the pixel.
- Without that permission the call answers `403` asking you to reconnect the Meta ads account.
- `partners[]` (`id`, `name`) are the pixel's shared agencies, read only.

**Removing a user** is not possible through Meta's API. The Business SDK has no delete on the pixel's `/assigned_users`, and re-assigning with no tasks answers "The parameter tasks is required".

Meta's `DELETE` answers "Unsupported delete request" (code 100, subcode 33). Zernio's `DELETE .../users/{userId}` answers `501`. Remove the user in Business Settings, Data sources, Pixels.

**Sharing with a new partner** is not possible either: `POST /{pixel}/agencies` answers "(#3) Application does not have the capability to make this API call".

## Custom conversions

A pixel's conversion events are its custom conversions. Manage them with `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags/{tagId}/events`.

Custom conversions live on the ad account. These calls read `adAccountId` (default: the pixel's owner ad account) and keep only the conversions that use this pixel. They have no `siteEventId`.

| Field | On create | On update |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| `name` | Required | Yes |
| `type` | A Meta custom conversion type: `PURCHASE`, `ADD_TO_CART`, `LEAD`, `COMPLETE_REGISTRATION`, `CONTENT_VIEW`, `INITIATED_CHECKOUT`, `SEARCH`, `SUBSCRIBE`, `OTHER` and the rest of `CustomConversion.CustomEventType` | No |
| `siteEvent` | Alternative to `type`: `purchase` becomes `PURCHASE` on the `Purchase` event, `page_view` becomes `OTHER` on `PageView` | No |
| `urlContains` | Adds a URL rule (the URL contains this text). Without a `siteEvent` it matches page loads, as Events Manager's URL-based conversions do | No |
| `defaultValue` | The conversion's default value | Yes |

The rule is built from those fields. The conversion matches the standard event behind `siteEvent` (or behind `type`), plus the URL condition when `urlContains` is set.

Meta's update takes only the name and default value. Changing `type`, `siteEvent` or `urlContains` answers `400`, so create a new conversion instead.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data } = await zernio.trackingtags.createTrackingTagEvent({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', tagId: '1729525464415281' },
  body: { name: 'Thank-you page purchase', siteEvent: 'purchase', urlContains: '/thank-you', defaultValue: 40 }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
data = client.tracking_tags.create_tracking_tag_event(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    tag_id="1729525464415281",
    name="Thank-you page purchase",
    site_event="purchase",
    url_contains="/thank-you",
    default_value=40,
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/1729525464415281/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "Thank-you page purchase", "siteEvent": "purchase", "urlContains": "/thank-you", "defaultValue": 40 }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "event": {
    "id": "1183640298476512",
    "name": "Thank-you page purchase",
    "type": "PURCHASE",
    "siteEvent": "purchase",
    "status": "active",
    "defaultValue": 40,
    "urlContains": "/thank-you"
  }
}
```

The create is idempotent by name. An active conversion with the same name on this pixel is returned instead of a duplicate.

`DELETE` archives the conversion (`state: "archived"`), because Meta has no hard delete for custom conversions. It stays readable with `status: "archived"`, and deleting an archived one again is a no-op.

[Conversion campaigns](/platforms/meta-ads/conversion-campaigns) can optimize for a custom conversion by its `id`.

## Diagnostics

`GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags/{tagId}/diagnostics` returns Meta's health checks for the pixel: the Dynamic Ads checks Events Manager shows.

Each entry in `checks[]` has `key`, `title`, `description` and `result`. When Meta suggests a fix, it also has an `actionUrl` into Events Manager.

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "checks": [
    {
      "key": "pixel_content_ids_match_catalog",
      "title": "Content IDs match catalog",
      "description": "The content IDs your pixel sends should match the IDs in your catalog.",
      "result": "passed",
      "actionUrl": "https://business.facebook.com/events_manager2/..."
    }
  ]
}
```

Diagnostics exist on Meta only; other platforms answer `501`.

## Install on a Shopify store

`POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags/{tagId}/install` puts the pixel on a [connected Shopify store](/platforms/shopify) through Zernio's Shopify app pixel. There are no theme edits and no code on the merchant's side.

`accountId` is the Meta ads account that owns the pixel. `storeAccountId` is the Shopify account.

The store then sends these events, each with an event id:

| Shopify event | Meta event | Data |
|---------------|------------|------|
| Page viewed | `PageView` | |
| Product viewed | `ViewContent` | variant as `content_ids`, `value`, `currency` |
| Added to cart | `AddToCart` | line total as `value`, `currency`, `contents` |
| Search submitted | `Search` | `search_string` |
| Checkout started | `InitiateCheckout` | every line, `num_items`, `value`, `currency` |
| Payment info submitted | `AddPaymentInfo` | as checkout started |
| Checkout completed | `Purchase` | order total as `value`, `currency`, `contents`, `order_id` |

`content_ids` are Shopify variant ids.

The Purchase event id is `shopify_order_{orderId}` (the numeric order id). Send a server-side Purchase for the same order through the [Conversions API](/products/conversions-api) with that `eventId`, and Meta deduplicates it.

Events follow the store's customer privacy settings. Where consent is required, the pixel fires only for visitors who allow marketing.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data } = await zernio.trackingtags.installTrackingTagOnStore({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', tagId: '1729525464415281' },
  body: { storeAccountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c3e' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
result = client.tracking_tags.install_tracking_tag_on_store(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    tag_id="1729525464415281",
    store_account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c3e",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/1729525464415281/install" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "storeAccountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c3e" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "install": {
    "storeAccountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c3e",
    "platform": "shopify",
    "shopDomain": "acme.myshopify.com",
    "tagPlatform": "metaads",
    "siteTagId": "1729525464415281",
    "installed": true,
    "installedTagId": "1729525464415281",
    "webPixelId": "2031620387",
    "tags": [
      { "platform": "metaads", "siteTagId": "1729525464415281" },
      { "platform": "tiktokads", "siteTagId": "D00IKHRC77UE0J0RTNHG" }
    ],
    "replacedTagId": null
  }
}
```

The call is idempotent. A store runs one Zernio web pixel that holds one tag per ad platform.

Installing a different Meta pixel replaces the previous one and names it in `replacedTagId`. The store's TikTok, Google, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X or OpenAI tags keep firing.

`GET` on the same path with `?storeAccountId=` returns the install status. `installedTagId` is whichever Meta pixel the store fires now, and `tags` is every Zernio tag on the store.

`DELETE` with `?storeAccountId=` removes the Meta pixel and leaves the other platforms' tags. Removing a pixel the store does not fire changes nothing and answers `409 invalid_resource_state`.

[Shopify tracking pixels](/platforms/shopify/tracking-pixels) has the event mapping for every platform.

### When the store must re-approve

Stores connected before 28 September 2026 have not granted the pixel permissions (`write_pixels`, `read_customer_events`).

On those, all three calls answer `409 reconnect_required` with a fresh consent link:

```json
{
  "error": "The Shopify store acme.myshopify.com has not granted write_pixels, read_customer_events. Send the merchant to details.authUrl to re-approve the Zernio app (the account id stays the same), then retry.",
  "type": "permission_error",
  "code": "reconnect_required",
  "param": "storeAccountId",
  "platform": "shopify",
  "details": {
    "missingScopes": ["write_pixels", "read_customer_events"],
    "authUrl": "https://acme.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize?client_id=..."
  }
}
```

Send the merchant to `details.authUrl`, or run the [Shopify connect](/platforms/shopify#connect) flow again with your own `redirect_url`. The store keeps its account id, so retry the install afterwards.

**Custom-app stores.** Stores connected with a custom-app Admin token get the same answer. A pixel belongs to the app that installs it, so those stores must connect through the Zernio app.

## Install on a WordPress site

The same endpoint puts the pixel on a [connected WordPress site](/platforms/wordpress) (WordPress.com or self-hosted). Pass the WordPress account as `storeAccountId`.

Zernio adds a Custom HTML widget to a widget area of the active theme. The widget holds the Meta pixel base code (`fbevents.js`, `init` with your pixel id, `PageView`).

Zernio then reads the widget back to confirm WordPress kept the `<script>` tag.

It picks a footer area when the theme has one, otherwise the first active area. Pass `sidebarId` to choose.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data } = await zernio.trackingtags.installTrackingTagOnStore({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', tagId: '1729525464415281' },
  body: { storeAccountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c4f' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
result = client.tracking_tags.install_tracking_tag_on_store(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    tag_id="1729525464415281",
    store_account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c4f",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/1729525464415281/install" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "storeAccountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c4f", "sidebarId": "sidebar-1" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "install": {
    "storeAccountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c4f",
    "platform": "wordpress",
    "siteUrl": "https://example.com",
    "tagPlatform": "metaads",
    "siteTagId": "1729525464415281",
    "installed": true,
    "method": "wordpress_widget",
    "widgetId": "custom_html-2",
    "sidebarId": "sidebar-1",
    "sidebarName": "Footer",
    "created": true,
    "homepageCheck": "found"
  }
}
```

The widget carries a Zernio marker, so the call is idempotent per pixel. Calling it again updates (or moves) the same widget and returns `created: false`.

Several pixels can run on one site, one widget each. Pixel code you pasted by hand is never touched.

`homepageCheck` reports whether the pixel appears in the homepage HTML:

- `found`
- `not_found`
- `unreachable`
- `skipped`, with `verifyHomepage: false`

`not_found` can simply be a page cache that has not refreshed yet. The widget read-back is the authoritative check.

`GET` with `?storeAccountId=` returns the install status plus:

- a read-only `preflight` (`ready`, `reason`, and the theme's widget areas in `sidebars`), so you can check a site before installing
- `tags`, every Zernio widget on the site with its platform and whether it is `active`

`DELETE` with `?storeAccountId=` removes every widget Zernio created for the pixel and reports `removed`.

### When WordPress cannot run the pixel

WordPress keeps a `<script>` tag only for users with the `unfiltered_html` capability.

When the site cannot run the pixel, Zernio removes anything it wrote. It answers `422 tracking_tag_install_blocked` with the cause in `details.reason`:

| `details.reason` | Cause |
|------------------|-------|
| `insufficient_permissions` | The connected user is not an Administrator (lacks `edit_theme_options`). |
| `wordpress_com_plan` | WordPress.com strips scripts on plans without plugin support. |
| `scripts_stripped` | The site removed the script: a multisite admin who is not a Super Admin, or `DISALLOW_UNFILTERED_HTML` is set. |
| `no_widget_areas` | The theme has no widget areas (block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five use the Site Editor). |
| `widgets_api_unavailable` | The site has no widgets REST API (WordPress older than 5.8, or disabled by a security plugin). |

```json
{
  "error": "This WordPress.com plan strips <script> tags from site content. On a Business or Commerce plan, install Meta's official \"Meta pixel for WordPress\" plugin (official-facebook-pixel) instead.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "code": "tracking_tag_install_blocked",
  "details": { "reason": "wordpress_com_plan" }
}
```

In each case the site owner can install Meta's official **Meta pixel for WordPress** plugin instead, or on a block theme add the pixel code to the footer template part with a Custom HTML block.

## Firing stats

`GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags/{tagId}/stats` returns aggregated event counts between `startTime` and `endTime` (Unix seconds).

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: stats } = await zernio.trackingtags.getTrackingTagStats({
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "platform": "metaads",
  "stats": {
    "aggregation": "event",
    "startTime": 1809216000,
    "endTime": 1809475200,
    "rows": [
      { "aggregation": "event", "data": [{ "value": 3 }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

Zernio echoes the query back and passes each row through untouched. A row holds Meta's own `AdsPixelStatsResult` for the aggregation you asked for.

Read the keys you get rather than coding against a fixed shape.

`aggregation` defaults to `event`. It also accepts `host`, `url`, `url_by_rule`, `pixel_fire`, `device_type`, `device_os`, `browser_type`, `had_pii`, `custom_data_field`, `match_keys`, `event_source`, `event_detection_method`, `event_processing_results`, `event_total_counts` and `event_value_count`.

Both time bounds are optional. Omit them for Meta's own default window.

## If it fails
A `403` means the connection has no ads access:

```json
{
  "error": "Ads add-on required"
}
```

Ads are included with usage-based billing. So this is either a legacy plan without ads or a Meta token missing the ads permissions.

Reconnect the account ([scopes](/guides/connecting-accounts#scopes)).

A `501 platform_not_supported` means the operation does not exist on the platform of the account you called. The [capability matrix](/guides/pixels#capability-matrix) lists what every platform supports.
